NKJV.1: So all the work that Solomon had done for the house of the LORD was finished; and Solomon brought in the things which his father David had dedicated: the silver and the gold and all the furnishings. And he put them in the treasuries of the house of God.
NKJV.2: Now Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the chief fathers of the children of Israel, in Jerusalem, that they might bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD up from the City of David, which is Zion.
NKJV.3: Therefore all the men of Israel assembled with the king at the feast, which was in the seventh month.
NKJV.4: So all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites took up the ark.
NKJV.5: Then they brought up the ark, the tabernacle of meeting, and all the holy furnishings that were in the tabernacle. The priests and the Levites brought them up.
NKJV.6: Also King Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel who were assembled with him before the ark, were sacrificing sheep and oxen that could not be counted or numbered for multitude.
NKJV.7: Then the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the temple, to the Most Holy Place, under the wings of the cherubim.
NKJV.8: For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles.
NKJV.9: The poles extended so that the ends of the poles of the ark could be seen from the holy place, in front of the inner sanctuary; but they could not be seen from outside. And they are there to this day.
NKJV.10: Nothing was in the ark except the two tablets which Moses put there at Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they had come out of Egypt.
NKJV.11: And it came to pass when the priests came out of the Most Holy Place (for all the priests who were present had sanctified themselves, without keeping to their divisions),
NKJV.12: and the Levites who were the singers, all those of Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, with their sons and their brethren, stood at the east end of the altar, clothed in white linen, having cymbals, stringed instruments and harps, and with them one hundred and twenty priests sounding with trumpets—
NKJV.13: indeed it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying: “For He is good, For His mercy endures forever,” that the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,
NKJV.14: so that the priests could not continue ministering because of the cloud; for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

NASB.1: Thus all the work that Solomon performed for the house of the LORD was finished. And Solomon brought in the things that David his father had dedicated, even the silver and the gold and all the utensils, [and] put [them] in the treasuries of the house of God.
NASB.2: Then Solomon assembled to Jerusalem the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' [households] of the sons of Israel, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the city of David, which is Zion.
NASB.3: All the men of Israel assembled themselves to the king at the feast, that is [in] the seventh month.
NASB.4: Then all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites took up the ark.
NASB.5: They brought up the ark and the tent of meeting and all the holy utensils which [were] in the tent; the Levitical priests brought them up.
NASB.6: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who were assembled with him before the ark, were sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
NASB.7: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the holy of holies, under the wings of the cherubim.
NASB.8: For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim made a covering over the ark and its poles.
NASB.9: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles of the ark could be seen in front of the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen outside; and they are there to this day.
NASB.10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets which Moses put [there] at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the sons of Israel, when they came out of Egypt.
NASB.11: When the priests came forth from the holy place (for all the priests who were present had sanctified themselves, without regard to divisions),
NASB.12: and all the Levitical singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and kinsmen, clothed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps and lyres, standing east of the altar, and with them one hundred and twenty priests blowing trumpets
NASB.13: in unison when the trumpeters and the singers were to make themselves heard with one voice to praise and to glorify the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice accompanied by trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and when they praised the LORD [saying,]'[He] indeed is good for His lovingkindness is everlasting,' then the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,
NASB.14: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

ESV.1: Thus all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. And Solomon brought in the things that David his father had dedicated, and stored the silver, the gold, and all the vessels in the treasuries of the house of God.
ESV.2: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' houses of the people of Israel, in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the city of David, which is Zion.
ESV.3: And all the men of Israel assembled before the king at the feast that is in the seventh month.
ESV.4: And all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites took up the ark.
ESV.5: And they brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the Levitical priests brought them up.
ESV.6: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who had assembled before him, were before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
ESV.7: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, in the inner sanctuary of the house, in the Most Holy Place, underneath the wings of the cherubim.
ESV.8: The cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim made a covering above the ark and its poles.
ESV.9: And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the Holy Place before the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from outside. And they are  there to this day.
ESV.10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the people of Israel, when they came out of Egypt.
ESV.11: And when the priests came out of the Holy Place (for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves, without regard to their divisions,
ESV.12: and all the Levitical singers, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, their sons and kinsmen, arrayed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, stood east of the altar with 120 priests who were trumpeters;
ESV.13: and it was the duty of the trumpeters and singers to make themselves heard in unison in praise and thanksgiving to the LORD), and when the song was raised, with trumpets and cymbals and other musical instruments, in praise to the LORD, “For he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever,”  the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,
ESV.14: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

AMP.1: Thus all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. He brought in the things that his father David had dedicated, and he put the silver and the gold and all the utensils in the treasuries of the house of God.
AMP.2: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' households of the Israelites, in Jerusalem to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD up from the City of David, which is Zion.
AMP.3: All the men of Israel gathered before the king at the feast in the seventh month.
AMP.4: And all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites took up the ark.
AMP.5: The Levitical priests brought up the ark, the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy utensils that were in the Tent.
AMP.6: And King Solomon and all the assembly of Israel who gathered together with him before the ark were sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
AMP.7: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, to the inner sanctuary of the house, into the Holy of Holies, under the wings of the cherubim;
AMP.8: for the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, making a covering above the ark and its carrying poles.
AMP.9: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles of the ark were visible from the front of the Holy of Holies (inner sanctuary), but were not visible from the outside. They are there to this day.
AMP.10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets [of the Ten Commandments] which Moses put there at Mount Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites, when they came out of Egypt.
AMP.11: When the priests came out of the Holy Place (for all the priests who were present had sanctified themselves [separating themselves from everything unclean], without regard to their assigned divisions),
AMP.12: and all of the Levitical singers, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, with their sons and relatives, clothed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres were standing at the east end of the altar, and with them a hundred and twenty priests blowing trumpets
AMP.13: in unison when the trumpeters and singers were to make themselves heard with one voice praising and thanking the LORD, and when they raised their voices accompanied by the trumpets and cymbals and [other] instruments of music, and when they praised the LORD, saying, "For He is good, for His mercy and lovingkindness endure forever," then the house of the LORD was filled with a cloud,
AMP.14: so that the priests could not remain standing to minister because of the cloud; for the glory and brilliance of the LORD filled the house of God.

WEB.1: Thus all the work that Solomon did for Yahweh’s house was finished. Solomon brought in the things that David his father had dedicated, even the silver, the gold, and all the vessels, and put them in the treasuries of God’s house.
WEB.2: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers’ households of the children of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of Yahweh’s covenant out of David’s city, which is Zion.
WEB.3: So all the men of Israel assembled themselves to the king at the feast, which was in the seventh month.
WEB.4: All the elders of Israel came. The Levites took up the ark;
WEB.5: and they brought up the ark, the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the Tent; these the priests the Levites brought up.
WEB.6: King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who were assembled to him, were before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or counted for multitude.
WEB.7: The priests brought in the ark of Yahweh’s covenant to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubim.
WEB.8: For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles above.
WEB.9: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary; but they were not seen outside; and it is there to this day.
WEB.10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets which Moses put at Horeb, when Yahweh made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of Egypt.
WEB.11: When the priests had come out of the holy place (for all the priests who were present had sanctified themselves, and didn’t keep their divisions;
WEB.12: also the Levites who were the singers, all of them, even Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and their brothers, arrayed in fine linen, with cymbals and stringed instruments and harps, stood at the east end of the altar, and with them one hundred twenty priests sounding with trumpets);
WEB.13: when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking Yahweh; and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised Yahweh, saying, “For he is good; for his loving kindness endures forever!”  then the house was filled with a cloud, even Yahweh’s house,
WEB.14: so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud; for Yahweh’s glory filled God’s house.

CSB17.1: So all the work Solomon did for the LORD’s temple was completed. Then Solomon brought the consecrated things of his father David — the silver, the gold, and all the utensils — and put them in the treasuries of God’s temple.
CSB17.2: At that time <sup>ⓑ</sup> Solomon assembled at Jerusalem the elders of Israel — all the tribal heads, the ancestral chiefs of the Israelites — in order to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD up from the city of David, <sup>ⓒ</sup> that is, Zion.
CSB17.3: So all the men of Israel were assembled in the king’s presence at the festival; this was in the seventh month. <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.4: All the elders of Israel came, and the Levites picked up the ark.
CSB17.5: They brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and the holy utensils that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites brought them up.
CSB17.6: King Solomon and the entire congregation of Israel who had gathered around him were in front of the ark sacrificing sheep, goats, and cattle that could not be counted or numbered because there were so many.
CSB17.7: The priests brought the ark of the LORD’s covenant to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the temple, to the most holy place, beneath the wings of the cherubim. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.8: And the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark so that the cherubim formed a cover above the ark and its poles.
CSB17.9: The poles were so long that their ends were seen from the holy place <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓔ</sup> in front of the inner sanctuary, but they were not seen from outside; they are still there today.
CSB17.10: Nothing was in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had put in it at Horeb, <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓕ</sup> where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
CSB17.11: Now all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves regardless of their divisions. <sup>ⓖ</sup> When the priests came out of the holy place,
CSB17.12: the Levitical singers dressed in fine linen and carrying cymbals, harps, and lyres <sup>ⓗ</sup> were standing east of the altar, and with them were 120 priests blowing trumpets. <sup>ⓘ</sup> The Levitical singers were descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun and their sons <sup>ⓙ</sup> and relatives.
CSB17.13:
The trumpeters and singers joined together to praise and thank the LORD with one voice. They raised their voices, accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, ⓚ in praise to the LORD: For he is good;
his faithful love endures forever. ⓛ
The temple, the LORD’s temple, was filled with a cloud. ⓜ
CSB17.14: And because of the cloud, the priests were not able to continue ministering, for the glory of the LORD filled God’s temple. <sup>ⓝ</sup>

NLT.1: So Solomon finished all his work on the Temple of the LORD. Then he brought all the gifts his father, David, had dedicated — the silver, the gold, and the various articles — and he stored them in the treasuries of the Temple of God.
NLT.2: Solomon then summoned to Jerusalem the elders of Israel and all the heads of tribes — the leaders of the ancestral families of Israel. They were to bring the Ark of the LORD’s Covenant to the Temple from its location in the City of David, also known as Zion.
NLT.3: So all the men of Israel assembled before the king at the annual Festival of Shelters, which is held in early autumn.
NLT.4: When all the elders of Israel arrived, the Levites picked up the Ark.
NLT.5: The priests and Levites brought up the Ark along with the special tent and all the sacred items that had been in it.
NLT.6: There, before the Ark, King Solomon and the entire community of Israel sacrificed so many sheep, goats, and cattle that no one could keep count!
NLT.7: Then the priests carried the Ark of the LORD’s Covenant into the inner sanctuary of the Temple — the Most Holy Place — and placed it beneath the wings of the cherubim.
NLT.8: The cherubim spread their wings over the Ark, forming a canopy over the Ark and its carrying poles.
NLT.9: These poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Holy Place, which is in front of the Most Holy Place, but not from the outside. They are still there to this day.
NLT.10: Nothing was in the Ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Mount Sinai, where the LORD made a covenant with the people of Israel when they left Egypt.
NLT.11: Then the priests left the Holy Place. All the priests who were present had purified themselves, whether or not they were on duty that day.
NLT.12: And the Levites who were musicians — Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and all their sons and brothers — were dressed in fine linen robes and stood at the east side of the altar playing cymbals, lyres, and harps. They were joined by 120 priests who were playing trumpets.
NLT.13:
The trumpeters and singers performed together in unison to praise and give thanks to the LORD. Accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments, they raised their voices and praised the LORD with these words: “He is good!
His faithful love endures forever!”
At that moment a thick cloud filled the Temple of the LORD.
NLT.14: The priests could not continue their service because of the cloud, for the glorious presence of the LORD filled the Temple of God.

MSG.1: That completed the work King Solomon did on The Temple of God. He then brought in the holy offerings of his father David, the silver and the gold and the artifacts. He placed them all in the treasury of God's Temple.
MSG.2: Bringing all this to a climax, Solomon got all the leaders together in Jerusalem—all the chiefs of tribes and the family patriarchs—to move the Chest of the Covenant of God from Zion and install it in The Temple.
MSG.3: All the men of Israel assembled before the king on the feast day of the seventh month, the Feast of Booths.
MSG.4: When all the leaders of Israel were ready, the Levites took up the Chest.
MSG.5: They carried the Chest, the Tent of Meeting, and all the sacred things in the Tent used in worship. The priests, all Levites, carried them.
MSG.6: King Solomon and the entire congregation of Israel were there before the Chest, worshiping and sacrificing huge numbers of sheep and cattle—so many that no one could keep track.
MSG.7: The priests brought the Chest of the Covenant of God to its place in the Inner Sanctuary, the Holy of Holies, under the wings of the cherubim.
MSG.8: The outspread wings of the cherubim formed a canopy over the Chest and its poles.
MSG.9: The ends of the poles were so long that they stuck out from the entrance of the Inner Sanctuary, but were not noticeable further out—they're still there today.
MSG.10: There was nothing in the Chest itself but the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb where God made a covenant with Israel after bringing them up from Egypt.
MSG.11: The priests then left the Holy Place. All the priests there were consecrated, regardless of rank or assignment;
MSG.12: and all the Levites who were musicians were there—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their families, dressed in their worship robes; the choir and orchestra assembled on the east side of the Altar and were joined by 120 priests blowing trumpets.
MSG.13:
The choir and trumpets made one voice of praise and thanks to God—orchestra and choir in perfect harmony singing and playing praise to God:
Yes! God is good!
His loyal love goes on forever!
Then a billowing cloud filled The Temple of God.
MSG.14: The priests couldn't even carry out their duties because of the cloud—the glory of God!—that filled The Temple of God.

NIV.2:
The Ark Brought to the Temple
Then Solomon summoned to Jerusalem the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes and the chiefs of the Israelite families, to bring up the ark of the Lord’s covenant from Zion, the City of David.
NIV.3: And all the men of Israel came together to the king at the time of the festival in the seventh month.
NIV.4: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites took up the ark,
NIV.5: and they brought up the ark and the Tent of Meeting and all the sacred furnishings in it. The priests, who were Levites, carried them up;
NIV.6: and King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel that had gathered about him were before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be recorded or counted.
NIV.7: The priests then brought the ark of the Lord’s covenant to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, and put it beneath the wings of the cherubim.
NIV.8: The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and covered the ark and its carrying poles.
NIV.9: These poles were so long that their ends, extending from the ark, could be seen from in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place; and they are still there today.
NIV.10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the Lord made a covenant with the Israelites after they came out of Egypt.

NIV.12: All the Levites who were musicians—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun and their sons and relatives—stood on the east side of the altar, dressed in fine linen and playing cymbals, harps and lyres. They were accompanied by 120 priests sounding trumpets.
NIV.13:
The trumpeters and singers joined in unison, as with one voice, to give praise and thanks to the Lord. Accompanied by trumpets, cymbals and other instruments, they raised their voices in praise to the Lord and sang:
“He is good;

NRSVCE.1: Thus all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. Solomon brought in the things that his father David had dedicated, and stored the silver, the gold, and all the vessels in the treasuries of the house of God.
NRSVCE.2: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the people of Israel, in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the city of David, which is Zion.
NRSVCE.3: And all the Israelites assembled before the king at the festival that is in the seventh month.
NRSVCE.4: And all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites carried the ark.
NRSVCE.5: So they brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.
NRSVCE.6: King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who had assembled before him, were before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be numbered or counted.
NRSVCE.7: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, in the inner sanctuary of the house, in the most holy place, underneath the wings of the cherubim.
NRSVCE.8: For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim made a covering above the ark and its poles.
NRSVCE.9: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place in front of the inner sanctuary; but they could not be seen from outside; they are there to this day.
NRSVCE.10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the people of Israel after they came out of Egypt.
NRSVCE.11: Now when the priests came out of the holy place (for all the priests who were present had sanctified themselves, without regard to their divisions),
NRSVCE.12: all the levitical singers, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, their sons and kindred, arrayed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, stood east of the altar with one hundred twenty priests who were trumpeters.
NRSVCE.13:
It was the duty of the trumpeters and singers to make themselves heard in unison in praise and thanksgiving to the LORD, and when the song was raised, with trumpets and cymbals and other musical instruments, in praise to the LORD, “For he is good,
for his steadfast love endures forever,”
the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,
NRSVCE.14: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud; for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

NET.1: When Solomon had finished constructing the LORD’s temple, he put the holy items that belonged to his father David (the silver, gold, and all the other articles) in the treasuries of God’s temple.
NET.2: Then Solomon convened Israel’s elders — all the leaders of the Israelite tribes and families — in Jerusalem, so they could witness the transferal of the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David (that is, Zion).
NET.3: All the men of Israel assembled before the king during the festival in the seventh month.
NET.4: When all Israel’s elders had arrived, the Levites lifted the ark.
NET.5: The priests and Levites carried the ark, the tent where God appeared to his people, and all the holy items in the tent.
NET.6: Now King Solomon and all the Israelites who had assembled with him went on ahead of the ark and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted or numbered.
NET.7: The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its assigned place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, in the most holy place under the wings of the cherubs.
NET.8: The cherubs’ wings extended over the place where the ark sat; the cherubs overshadowed the ark and its poles.
NET.9: The poles were so long their ends extending out from the ark were visible from in front of the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from beyond that point. They have remained there to this very day.
NET.10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets Moses had placed there in Horeb. (It was there that the LORD made an agreement with the Israelites after he brought them out of the land of Egypt.)
NET.11: The priests left the holy place. All the priests who participated had consecrated themselves, no matter which division they represented.
NET.12: All the Levites who were musicians, including Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives, wore linen. They played cymbals and stringed instruments as they stood east of the altar. They were accompanied by 120 priests who blew trumpets.
NET.13: The trumpeters and musicians played together, praising and giving thanks to the LORD. Accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments, they loudly praised the LORD, singing: “Certainly he is good; certainly his loyal love endures!” Then a cloud filled the LORD’s temple.
NET.14: The priests could not carry out their duties because of the cloud; the LORD’s splendor filled God’s temple.
